features.name: Enhanced Shopify Log Entries View
features.description: The new default view in Shopify log entries displays additional columns showing request and response information to distinguish between different types of synchronization (customer, order, product), and includes an error indicator checkbox to identify failed synchronization attempts.

features.name: Request ID for Shopify Support
features.description: Request IDs are provided in log entries to help identify specific request-response pairs when contacting Shopify support, enabling faster identification and more detailed information.

features.name: User Error Section in Log Responses
features.description: Log responses now contain a user error section that details what failed on the Shopify side when submitting data, such as invalid phone numbers or blank required fields.

features.name: Logging Mode Option Field
features.description: The logging mode on the Shopify shop card has been transformed from a boolean on/off toggle into an option field with three modes: disabled, fully enabled, and error only (default), which reduces log pollution by only recording errors.

features.name: Log Retention Policies
features.description: Retention policies now automatically clean up Shopify log entries by default on a monthly basis, removing entries older than one month.

features.name: Shopify Data Capture Retention Policy
features.description: A retention policy for Shopify data capture logs is available but disabled by default.

features.name: User Error Support in Product Queries
features.description: Product and other entity queries have been modified to return user error sections when errors occur, helping with troubleshooting of product synchronization issues.

features.name: Business Central Fulfillment Service Support
features.description: Full support for Business Central fulfillment service has been enabled, allowing Shopify to be configured to use Business Central fulfillment with external systems, supporting both multiple fulfillment locations and configurations where Shopify locations are managed entirely by Business Central.

features.name: SKU Requirement for Fulfillment Service
features.description: When Business Central fulfillment service is selected in Shopify, the SKU field is required and cannot be blank, enforcing data validation consistency between Business Central and Shopify.

features.name: End of Support Indicator
features.description: The Shopify shop card now displays an end of support date field that informs users when their current API version will no longer be supported, encouraging timely upgrades of Business Central.

features.name: Shopify API Quarterly Versioning
features.description: Shopify releases new API versions quarterly (four times per year), with each version supported for one year. Business Central updates its connector to keep up with current versions in releases and minor updates.

features.name: Foreground Synchronization Debugging
features.description: Users can disable background job queue synchronization and run synchronizations in the foreground to immediately see errors and copy detailed error information including call stacks for easier troubleshooting.

features.name: Shopify Orders to Import Buffer Table
features.description: The Shopify orders to import feature functions as a buffer table allowing users to manually manage and control which orders are imported from Shopify, with the ability to retrieve orders modified after a specific date or reset the date from Shopify admin.
caveats: Requires manual action to retrieve orders
Date can be reset from Shopify admin

features.name: Get Orders to Import Action
features.description: An action that retrieves orders which were modified after a specific date from Shopify. Downloads additional order information including header, payments, transactions, shipments, lines, returns, and refunds.
caveats: Downloads multiple types of data which takes time
Initial import is fast but full import requires additional download

features.name: Has Error Field in Order Import
features.description: A field in the Shopify orders to import table that displays errors encountered during order import. System shows error details at the bottom for troubleshooting.
caveats: Error reproduction depends on connector stability

features.name: Retrieve Shopify Data Inspection
features.description: Functionality allowing users to inspect the exact data received from Shopify for headers, lines, shipping costs, transactions, and fulfillment. Helps determine if problems originate from Shopify data or connector parsing.
caveats: Mainly useful for troubleshooting rather than routine exploration

features.name: Shopify JSON URL Inspection Technique
features.description: A method to view Shopify order data in JSON format by appending 'JSON' to the Shopify order URL. Useful for comparing Shopify data representation with Business Central data and understanding discounts and item variants.
caveats: Helps identify whether missing data is from Shopify or configuration issue

features.name: Role Center Shopify Activities Status Fields
features.description: Two new fields in the Role Center Shopify activities section showing the status of shipment synchronization - whether shipments are pending or failed. Provides actionable information for troubleshooting.
caveats: Requires exploration of underlying issues when failures occur

features.name: Shopify Fulfillment ID Field in Document
features.description: A field showing the Shopify fulfillment ID on the Business Central document, which can be 0, -1 if error, or an actual value. The value -1 can be manually changed to 0 to reset error state.
caveats: Cannot be edited when it has an actual value
Changing -1 to 0 is documented but intentionally confusing

features.name: Improved Logging with Configurable Detail Levels
features.description: Enhanced logging system providing more powerful and detailed logs when necessary, while using less space when details are not needed. Dramatically cleaner interface.

features.name: Shopify API Versioning Management
features.description: The Shopify connector handles API versioning automatically. Users just need to stay updated without worrying about version compatibility.

features.name: Multi-Shop Import Routing
features.description: Users can connect multiple Business Central shop cards to a single Shopify account and route imported orders to specific shops based on filters like tags or other criteria, allowing flexible order parsing and processing.
caveats: Requires manual selection of destination shop during import

quotes.text: With the new upgrade, the default view looks a bit better.
quotes.why_it_matters: Indicates the log view UI has been significantly improved in this release to help with troubleshooting.

quotes.text: And to help you to talk to Shopify support, you need to use a request ID.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the new capability to provide Shopify support with specific request identifiers for faster issue resolution.

quotes.text: Now logging mode transformed from the boolean on and off into the option field.
quotes.why_it_matters: Describes a design change that gives users more granular control over log collection to reduce noise.

quotes.text: Be aware that already before this release in one of the minor updates, we enabled full support for business central fulfillment service.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies that fulfillment service support was delivered in an earlier minor update, not this release.

quotes.text: Every quarter they release a new version of the API. So, four times per year, there is a new version. And each version is
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes the Shopify API versioning cadence and support window that drives connector update requirements.

quotes.text: If synchronization is running in the foreground, then you don't actually see any feedback when you execute synchronization.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains a troubleshooting technique for debugging synchronization issues in real-time rather than through job queue logs.

quotes.text: Shopify orders to import. It's not just a filtering opportunity. It is in reality the buffer table.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies that the orders to import feature is a buffer mechanism providing users manual control over order imports.

quotes.text: It's not just a filtering opportunity. It is in reality the buffer table.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the dual purpose of the Shopify orders to import feature as both a filter and a working table for order troubleshooting.

quotes.text: If I will press it, I will get orders which were modified after some specific date.
quotes.why_it_matters: Describes the mechanism for retrieving orders from Shopify for troubleshooting, allowing users to control what data is imported.

quotes.text: Header, fully payments, transactions, shipments, lines, returns, refunds, like a lot of stuff.
quotes.why_it_matters: Specifies the comprehensive data types downloaded during order import, showing the scope of the synchronization process.

quotes.text: Now you can see like what exactly we received from Shopify. So now you can understand if it's problem about data which we received
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the purpose of data inspection as a diagnostic tool to isolate whether problems originate from Shopify or the Business Central connector.

quotes.text: And then in the URL you just add JSON. Now you can see like representation of Shopify.
quotes.why_it_matters: Provides a practical technique for comparing Shopify data directly with Business Central data, useful for troubleshooting discrepancies.

quotes.text: And it can be 0, -1 if it's some error, or the actual value. If it has an actual value, then all good.
quotes.why_it_matters: Defines the meaning of fulfillment ID values as a key indicator of synchronization status and error conditions.

quotes.text: Shopify API versioning. No need to worry. Just stay updated.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies that API versioning is handled automatically, reducing operational burden for users maintaining the integration.
